scenes.title: Reconciliation & Data Auditing
scenes.subtitle: Proving data matches across systems
scenes.narration: Reconciliation and auditing verify that data agrees across systems and remains provably correct over time.

scenes.heading: What reconciliation checks
bullets: Row counts match between source and target
Key sets are identical with no missing records
Timing windows are aligned across systems
scenes.narration: Reconciliation confirms that the number of rows in the source matches the target, catching dropped or duplicated records. It compares the actual set of keys to find records present in one system but not the other. It also checks that aggregate totals like financial balances agree, and that both sides cover the same time window.

scenes.heading: A reconciliation run
steps: Extract control totals from the source
Compute the same totals on the target
Investigate breaks and log the audit result
scenes.narration: A run begins by extracting control totals such as counts and sums from the authoritative source. The same totals are computed independently on the target system. The two are compared and any difference is quantified, and every break is investigated while the outcome is written to an audit log for traceability.

scenes.heading: Reconciling two systems in SQL
scenes.code:
-- Compare counts and sums between source and target
SELECT 'source' AS side, COUNT(*) AS row_ct, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM source.orders
WHERE load_date = CURRENT_DATE
UNION ALL
SELECT 'target', COUNT(*), SUM(amount)
FROM target.orders
WHERE load_date = CURRENT_DATE;

-- Keys present in source but missing from target
SELECT s.order_id
FROM source.orders s
LEFT JOIN target.orders t ON s.order_id = t.order_id
WHERE t.order_id IS NULL;
scenes.narration: The first query pulls matching control totals from both sides so their row counts and amount sums can be compared directly. Any mismatch in either figure signals a reconciliation break to investigate. The second query performs an anti-join to list keys that exist in the source but never made it to the target, pinpointing exactly which records were lost.

scenes.text: Reconcile with control totals and key comparisons, and log every audit so correctness is provable, not assumed.
scenes.narration: Reconciliation gives you evidence that systems agree rather than a hopeful assumption. An audit trail turns that evidence into something you can defend to finance and regulators.
